questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A highly esteemed university with courses that are relevant to my education. A destination with an interesting culture. An English-speaking country

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Quite easy. I was a bit confused though, because I thought there were many different channels where information was given, eg. KUmail, Quercus, UofT mail, etc. and you had to check them all to make sure you didn't miss anything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There was only an online orientation. It would have been nice with a physical one.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found an appartment on AirBnB. It was quite easy, but quite expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is really nice to live close to campus. There is OK public transit, but I enjoyed being able to walk to and from campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was no housing available on campus for exchange students staying for less than a year.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can begin checking out courses early, but be aware that they may change from year to year. Mine were pretty much the same as last year though. Then when the final course list is pusblished, you sign up for a lecture period and possibly a lab class, depending on the course. You are responsible for ensuring your courses don't overlap.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I believe there was an e-mail you could contact, though I didn't need any help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You should sign up early to avoid getting waitlisted. You can sign up for 1 or 2 more courses than you want, either as back-up or if you want to check them out before deciding, because the deadline for dropping a courses is after the first week of classes,

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Around the same level of difficulty.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Lectures were kind of the same, but there were a lot more assignments and tests. The grade for each course is split over multiple assignments, mid-term exams and a final exam or assignment. My exams were all written in hand, with a lot of memorization required.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: GGR334H1: Water Resource Management, GGR347H1: Efficient Use of Energy, GGR375H1: Introduction to Programming in GIS, GGR415H1: Advanced Remote Sensing

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All my courses were pretty great, but especially GGR334H1 and GGR347H1 (though there was a lot of memorization for the tests)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Taxes on food.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries were more expensive than in DK. Clothes and other stuff were a bit less expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Lots of nice clubs and fitness classes.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Clubs (creative, sport clubs, language and culture clubs), fitness classes, gyms, pool, skating rink.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The fitness classes, especially barre. The outdoor club goes on trips about every other weekend and has some other activities that were very nice.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Algonquin National Park - rent a car and stay at Wolfden Hostel, one of the nicest and coziest hostels I've ever stayed at. Fly to Nova Scotia - has beautiful, rugged nature. Take the train to Montreal.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: They were more outgoing and extrovert than in Denmark. It took some getting used to, but was actually quite nice. Most Canadians are quite friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join some clubs. It is quite difficult making friends in class, especially if you are taking higher-level courses, since most other students already have a social circle by then.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really anything.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their friendliness. That the city was very multicultural with lots of different things to do including foods to try.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Look for housing early, there are a couple of off-campus colleges you can apply to. Join some of the clubs early on. Attend all lectures and take good notes.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Grocieries are expensive, but you can get vegetables and fruits for cheap in some of the Asian supermarkets. Bulk Barn is another great shop to check out.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improving my English, adapting to another culture, great courses.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
